evals.name: namespace-isolation
evals.prompt: Explain what a Chronicle namespace isolates and what is shared, and what that means for (a) a reactor on BookingConfirmed, (b) a unique constraint on registration number, (c) sequence numbers, (d) erasing a person's data who exists in two tenants. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Per namespace: sequences, observers, read models, jobs, constraint state, encryption keys. Reactors fire once per namespace; two tenants can hold the same unique value; sequence numbers are independent; erasure is one call per namespace.
assertions: States a reactor fires once per namespace that has the event, independently, not once globally.
States two tenants can hold the same unique value without violating a uniqueness constraint because constraint state is per namespace.
States sequence numbers are independent per namespace, so a sequence number only has meaning together with its namespace.
States erasure spanning tenants is one call per namespace and completing only some is an incomplete erasure.

evals.name: custom-resolver
evals.prompt: Write a C# IEventStoreNamespaceResolver that maps the current tenant from an injected `ITenantAccessor` (with `CurrentTenant` possibly null) to a Chronicle namespace, falling back to the default. Also say how registration picks resolvers when two are registered. Give the code in your reply; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: A class implementing the single synchronous Resolve() returning EventStoreNamespaceName, defaulting to EventStoreNamespaceName.Default, not caching the tenant; registration selects exactly one winner rather than a chain.
assertions: Implements IEventStoreNamespaceResolver with a synchronous Resolve() returning EventStoreNamespaceName.
Falls back to EventStoreNamespaceName.Default when no tenant is resolved.
Does not cache the tenant inside the resolver, which is registered as a singleton while the event store is scoped.
States registration selects exactly one winner (builder-set resolver, then the client-options resolver type, then the default) and is not a priority chain.

evals.name: second-tenant-code-rules
evals.prompt: Review this single-tenant code for a future second tenant: events carry a `TenantId` property; a singleton `BookingCache` holds an `IEventStore` captured at startup and a static dictionary of bookings; a nightly job calls `GetEventStore(name)` with no namespace. List the problems and fixes. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Remove tenant id from events because the namespace is the tenant; singletons must not hold tenant-scoped state and caches must key by tenant; background jobs must pass the namespace explicitly.
assertions: Says events should not carry a tenant identifier because the namespace is the tenant and a property creates a second source of truth that can disagree.
Says a singleton holding an event store pins to the namespace of the root scope and returns empty results rather than failing.
Says any cache of tenant data must include the tenant in its key.
Says a background job has no request to resolve from, so it must pass the namespace explicitly.

evals.name: tenant-resolution-facts
evals.prompt: A developer says 'use Chronicle's TenantNamespaceResolver and an ICanResolveNamespace; if no resolver is configured Chronicle will isolate tenants by header anyway'. Correct them. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: TenantNamespaceResolver is an example you write yourself in Chronicle docs (Arc has its own); ICanResolveNamespace and INamespaceResolver do not exist, the contract is IEventStoreNamespaceResolver; without a resolver everything lands in Default with no isolation.
assertions: States the contract is IEventStoreNamespaceResolver and that ICanResolveNamespace and INamespaceResolver do not exist.
States TenantNamespaceResolver is not a Chronicle type but an example resolver you write yourself.
States that with no resolver configured every tenant lands in the Default namespace and there is no isolation.
